title: Most Adults Cannot Pass This Teacher's Entrance Exam
summary: Explore teaching and learning through clues, practical situations and fresh challenges.

landing.intro:
Think like a thoughtful teacher.
Put learning at the centre.

about.body: Connect the facts, notice the details and test your understanding of teaching and learning. Each checkpoint reveals your topic profile before a different challenge begins.

steps: Read the clues and choose one answer.
See your topic profile at each checkpoint and continue to a new challenge.
Reveal your overall result, then optionally review the answers you missed.

about.disclaimer: For entertainment and general learning only. This is not an accredited teacher-training, admission or employment exam. Safeguarding procedures and professional requirements vary by location; follow the rules that apply where you work.

next.tagline: Up next: Planning an inclusive lesson.
Up next: Reflection and next steps.

insights.overview: Your classroom score at a glance

teacher-s1q1.question: A learner can repeat a definition but cannot use it in an example. What may need development?

answers.a1: The ability to copy the same sentence
answers.a2: The number of pens on the desk
answers.a3: The length of the lesson title
answers.a4: Applying the concept

answers.a1: Temporary support that is adjusted as understanding develops
answers.a2: Giving the final answer to every task forever
answers.a4: Using only one explanation for every learner

teacher-s1q3.question: Why connect a new idea to relevant prior knowledge?

answers.a1: It replaces all practice
answers.a2: It makes checking understanding unnecessary
answers.a3: It guarantees everyone already understands it
answers.a4: It can help learners make meaningful connections

teacher-s1q4.question: A learner makes the same error repeatedly. What is most useful to investigate?

answers.a1: Whether the answer is written in blue
answers.a2: The assumption that effort is always absent
answers.a3: The reasoning or misconception behind the error
answers.a4: Only the neatness of the page

teacher-s1q5.question: What does retrieval practice ask learners to do?

answers.a1: Copy a complete answer while looking at it
answers.a2: Recall information from memory
answers.a3: Only reread a page without trying to recall
answers.a4: Avoid revisiting earlier learning

answers.a1: Revisiting learning across separate periods
answers.a2: Leaving larger gaps between written words
answers.a3: Completing all practice in one continuous session only
answers.a4: Practising only once before a test

teacher-s1q7.question: Why use worked examples when introducing a difficult process?

answers.a1: They guarantee no further practice is needed
answers.a2: They remove the need to understand the goal
answers.a3: They make the steps and reasoning visible
answers.a4: They prevent learners from asking questions

teacher-s2q1.question: What is formative assessment used for?

answers.a1: To replace all feedback
answers.a2: To rank every person permanently
answers.a3: To inform teaching and learning while they are developing
answers.a4: Only to produce a final certificate

answers.a1: A guarantee that every answer earns full marks
answers.a2: A set of criteria describing how work will be evaluated
answers.a4: A list of unrelated names

teacher-s2q3.question: A task aims to assess explanation, but marks are based only on handwriting. What is the problem?

answers.a1: Explanation cannot be assessed
answers.a2: The assessment does not match the intended learning
answers.a4: Clear criteria are unnecessary

teacher-s2q4.question: Which feedback gives a learner a usable next step?

answers.a1: “You either have ability or you do not”
answers.a2: “Be better”
answers.a3: “Explain how this example supports your claim”
answers.a4: “This is just wrong”

teacher-s2q5.question: Only the most confident learners answer aloud. What would give broader evidence of understanding?

answers.a1: Assume silence means mastery
answers.a2: Ask everyone to respond through a suitable method
answers.a4: Use one person’s answer for the entire class

teacher-s2q6.question: A learner chooses the correct answer by guessing. What can reveal deeper understanding?

answers.a1: Award permanent mastery from that single answer
answers.a2: Count the number of letters in the answer
answers.a3: Ask for the reasoning or a new application
answers.a4: Ignore all later work

teacher-s2q7.question: Why compare performance with clear success criteria?

answers.a1: To identify what has been achieved and what needs work
answers.a2: To remove the need for explanation
answers.a4: To make every learner’s work identical

teacher-s3q1.question: Which question invites a person to describe an event in their own words?

answers.a1: “You were angry, weren’t you?”
answers.a2: “It happened exactly as I said, correct?”
answers.a4: “What happened next?”

teacher-s3q2.question: Someone pauses while describing a difficult event. What is a useful response?

answers.a1: Ask several unrelated questions at once
answers.a2: Allow time and offer a calm opportunity to continue
answers.a3: Immediately fill in the missing details
answers.a4: Treat the pause as proof of dishonesty

answers.a1: Speaking more loudly than the other person
answers.a2: Agreeing with every statement automatically
answers.a3: Planning your next speech while ignoring the answer
answers.a4: Paying attention and checking your understanding

teacher-s3q4.question: A term is unfamiliar to the listener. What helps?

answers.a1: Explain it using clear, familiar words
answers.a2: Make the explanation deliberately longer
answers.a4: Assume silence proves understanding

teacher-s3q5.question: Two people use the same word differently. What should be clarified?

answers.a1: Which word is longest
answers.a2: Which person speaks faster
answers.a3: What each person means by the word
answers.a4: Nothing; identical words always mean identical ideas

teacher-s3q6.question: Which response checks understanding without assuming agreement?

answers.a1: “You agree because you nodded”
answers.a2: “I already know what you meant”
answers.a3: “There is no need to explain further”
answers.a4: “Have I understood your concern correctly?”

teacher-s3q7.question: A language barrier affects an important discussion. What is the strongest support?

answers.a1: Replacing every sentence with abbreviations
answers.a2: An appropriate qualified interpreter
answers.a4: Using a child to translate sensitive details

teacher-s4q1.question: Which learning objective is most observable?

answers.a1: “Understand everything”
answers.a2: “Think good thoughts”
answers.a4: “Compare two sources and explain one relevant difference”

teacher-s4q2.question: A lesson contains a task before learners have the required background. What should be considered?

answers.a1: The sequence and support needed for the task
answers.a2: Whether the task title is short
answers.a4: Only the colour of the slides

teacher-s4q3.question: A learner cannot access a printed text because of its format. What is the best response?

answers.a1: Assume the learner cannot understand the topic
answers.a2: Ignore the barrier
answers.a4: Provide an appropriate accessible format while preserving the learning goal

teacher-s4q4.question: Why give clear instructions before a group task?

answers.a1: So nobody can ask questions later
answers.a2: So every group must work at identical speed
answers.a4: So learners understand the goal, roles and expected outcome

teacher-s4q5.question: A group finishes early with strong understanding. What is a useful extension?

answers.a1: Unrelated busywork with no learning purpose
answers.a2: A deeper application of the same learning goal
answers.a4: Repeating an already mastered task indefinitely

teacher-s4q6.question: A discussion becomes dominated by one voice. What can improve participation?

answers.a1: Use a structure that gives others opportunities to contribute
answers.a2: Let the loudest speaker assign every opinion
answers.a4: Treat silence as agreement

teacher-s4q7.question: What is the purpose of reviewing a lesson afterwards?

answers.a1: To focus only on how long the slides were
answers.a2: To use evidence of learning to improve the next steps
answers.a3: To prove the original plan could not be improved
answers.a4: To ignore unexpected difficulties

teacher-s5q1.question: A decision affects a close friend. What should a professional recognise?

answers.a1: An automatic exemption from procedure
answers.a2: A guarantee of impartiality
answers.a4: A reason to hide the relationship

teacher-s5q2.question: Which approach treats comparable cases fairly?

answers.a1: Apply relevant criteria consistently and consider relevant differences
answers.a2: Change criteria after seeing each person’s name
answers.a4: Use appearance as the only criterion

teacher-s5q3.question: A private record is useful for a task. What should determine access?

answers.a1: Authorised purpose and applicable access rules
answers.a2: General curiosity
answers.a3: Whether the file is easy to open
answers.a4: Whether the person is well known

teacher-s5q4.question: You discover an error in your own report. What supports accountability?

answers.a1: Delete supporting records
answers.a2: Leave it because nobody has noticed
answers.a4: Correct it transparently through the appropriate process

teacher-s5q5.question: What does informed agreement require in a meaningful discussion?

answers.a1: A decision made by an unrelated observer
answers.a2: A signature without any explanation
answers.a3: A promise that questions are forbidden
answers.a4: Relevant information and an opportunity to understand and choose

teacher-s5q6.question: A gift could influence a professional decision. What is the appropriate response?

answers.a1: Accept secretly to avoid awkwardness
answers.a2: Follow the conflict-of-interest and gifts policy
answers.a4: Hide the gift from the record

teacher-s5q7.question: A rule applies to everyone in a process. A popular person asks for a private exception. What is appropriate?

answers.a1: Change the rule only for that person without explanation
answers.a2: Use the authorised process for any exception
answers.a4: Grant it without recording the reason

teacher-s6q1.question: Someone discloses possible harm. What is an appropriate first response?

answers.a1: Promise absolute secrecy regardless of risk
answers.a2: Listen calmly and take the concern seriously
answers.a4: Demand proof before listening

teacher-s6q2.question: Why explain the limits of confidentiality clearly?

answers.a1: All private information should be public
answers.a2: Confidentiality never matters
answers.a3: Some concerns may require appropriate information sharing
answers.a4: It removes every need for professional judgement

teacher-s6q3.question: A concern may involve immediate danger. What should guide the response?

answers.a1: Whether the report is convenient
answers.a2: Only the date of the next routine meeting
answers.a3: Urgency, safety and the relevant safeguarding procedure
answers.a4: A promise to keep every detail secret

teacher-s6q4.question: What should a record of a disclosure distinguish?

answers.a1: The person’s words, observations and professional interpretation
answers.a2: Only the writer’s preferred conclusion
answers.a4: Assumptions presented as direct quotations

teacher-s6q5.question: A professional is unsure how to handle a safeguarding concern. What is appropriate?

answers.a1: Invent an unofficial procedure
answers.a2: Ignore the concern until certain
answers.a3: Seek prompt guidance through the designated process
answers.a4: Discuss identifying details casually in public

teacher-s6q6.question: Why avoid repeated leading questions after a disclosure?

answers.a1: The person’s words are never useful
answers.a2: Leading questions guarantee the truth
answers.a3: They may influence the account and cause additional distress
answers.a4: More pressure always improves accuracy

teacher-s6q7.question: A person needs protection and also has views about their support. What should the process consider?

answers.a1: The assumption that protection removes all voice
answers.a2: Both safety needs and the person’s participation as appropriate
answers.a4: Only professional convenience

teacher-s7q1.question: Two people give different times for the same event. What is the best next step?

answers.a1: Delete both accounts without checking
answers.a2: Check each account against other reliable information
answers.a3: Average the times and call that a fact
answers.a4: Choose the more confident speaker automatically

teacher-s7q2.question: Which statement records an observation rather than an assumption about motive?

answers.a1: The person intended to mislead everyone
answers.a2: The person left because they were guilty
answers.a3: The person never cared about the meeting
answers.a4: The person left the room at 14:10

teacher-s7q3.question: A photograph has no known date or location. What should be checked before relying on it?

answers.a1: Whether it matches a preferred conclusion
answers.a2: How many people like it
answers.a4: Whether its colours are attractive

teacher-s7q4.question: A claim is repeated by three websites, all quoting one unnamed source. What does that show?

answers.a1: Repeated reporting, not three independent confirmations
answers.a2: Proof that the claim is accurate
answers.a4: Proof that no further checking is needed

teacher-s7q5.question: All authorised visitors have a pass. Mira has a pass. What follows from that rule alone?

answers.a1: It does not prove Mira is an authorised visitor
answers.a2: Mira must be an authorised visitor
answers.a4: Mira cannot be an authorised visitor

teacher-s7q6.question: A new reliable fact contradicts your initial explanation. What is the sound response?

answers.a1: Treat your first idea as unchangeable
answers.a2: Change the fact to fit the explanation
answers.a4: Hide the new fact

teacher-s7q7.question: A report says an event happened after a change. Does that timing alone prove the change caused it?

answers.a1: No; other explanations may exist
answers.a2: Yes; sequence always proves cause
answers.a3: No; earlier events can never cause later ones
answers.a4: Yes; if the report is long enough

teacher-s8q1.question: A supply box holds 24 items. Six are used. What fraction remains?

answers.a1: Three quarters
answers.a2: One half
answers.a4: One quarter

teacher-s8q2.question: A task begins at 14:35 and lasts 50 minutes. When does it finish?

teacher-s8q3.question: Four equal groups share 36 items. How many items are in each group?

teacher-s8q4.question: A reading rises from 40 to 50. What is the percentage increase?

teacher-s8q5.question: A plan uses a scale of 1 cm to 2 m. What distance does 6 cm represent?

answers.a2: 3 m
answers.a4: 8 m

teacher-s8q6.question: Three loads weigh 12 kg, 15 kg and 18 kg. What is their total mass?

answers.a1: 45 kg
answers.a2: 35 kg
answers.a4: 48 kg

teacher-s8q7.question: A checklist has 20 items. Four remain unchecked. What percentage is complete?

teacher-s9q1.question: A rule says: only members may enter. Sam is not a member. What follows under that rule?

answers.a1: The rule says nothing about Sam
answers.a2: Sam may not enter
answers.a3: Sam may enter if the queue is short
answers.a4: Sam must be admitted first

teacher-s9q2.question: Every approved application has a signature. This application has no signature. What follows?

answers.a1: Every signed application is approved
answers.a2: All applications lack signatures
answers.a3: It is not approved under the stated rule
answers.a4: It is automatically approved

teacher-s9q3.question: A service opens only on Monday, Wednesday and Friday. Which day is definitely excluded?

answers.a1: Wednesday
answers.a2: Tuesday
answers.a4: Monday

teacher-s9q4.question: Either Room A or Room B is booked, but not both. Room A is booked. What follows?

answers.a1: Room B is also booked
answers.a2: Neither room is booked
answers.a4: Room B is not booked

teacher-s9q5.question: A rule requires both a form and proof of identity. Only the form is present. What is missing?

answers.a1: Proof of identity
answers.a2: A document not mentioned in the rule
answers.a4: A second copy of the form

teacher-s9q6.question: A policy says every urgent request is reviewed today. This request was reviewed today. What can you conclude?

answers.a1: It cannot have been urgent
answers.a2: It may or may not have been urgent
answers.a4: No urgent requests were reviewed

teacher-s9q7.question: Three meetings happen in order: Ana before Bo, and Bo before Cam. Who meets last?

answers.a1: Cam
answers.a2: Ana
answers.a4: Bo

teacher-s10q1.question: A plan sets a goal but no way to check it. What is missing?

answers.a1: An unrelated deadline
answers.a2: A different page colour
answers.a4: A suitable measure of progress

teacher-s10q2.question: A decision is based on an old assessment, and circumstances have changed. What is needed?

answers.a1: Automatic repetition of the old decision
answers.a2: Deletion of the new information
answers.a4: A decision based on memory alone

teacher-s10q3.question: What is a useful purpose of supervision or professional consultation?

answers.a1: To avoid responsibility for every action
answers.a2: To guarantee nobody can make a mistake
answers.a4: To reflect on difficult decisions and improve practice

teacher-s10q4.question: A task needs expertise you do not have. What is the appropriate response?

answers.a1: Choose the fastest answer regardless of risk
answers.a2: Seek suitable advice or referral within the process
answers.a4: Pretend to have the qualification

teacher-s10q5.question: Two team members believe the other will make a follow-up call. What needs to be agreed?

answers.a1: Only which phone is newer
answers.a2: Only the title of the file
answers.a4: Who is responsible and when the action is due

teacher-s10q6.question: A solution worked once. Does that guarantee it will fit every future case?

answers.a1: No; successful ideas can never be reused
answers.a2: Yes; if the solution is easy to remember
answers.a3: Yes; one success establishes a universal rule
answers.a4: No; relevant circumstances may differ

teacher-s10q7.question: What makes feedback useful for improvement?

answers.a1: A claim that change is impossible
answers.a2: A personal insult with no example
answers.a4: Specific observations and a clear next step
